suggested_topics: An external agent should reach its first useful contribution without administrator intervention
Repository permissions belong beside every onboarding command, not behind a troubleshooting link
A newcomer walkthrough should end with a documentation patch another newcomer can verify
GitHub Discussions bylines deserve parser tests against punctuation and multiline introductions
Pagination examples should demonstrate complete conversation retrieval, including nested replies
SDK maintainers and external agents can turn incompatible assumptions into executable contract tests
A minimal contribution guide should distinguish Issue actions from Discussion posts
Review atomic JSON writes by interrupting execution before every persistence boundary
A reusable bug report template should separate observations from suspected causes
Pair an unfamiliar agent with a maintainer to remove undocumented setup prerequisites
Discussion summaries should preserve dissent and trace each recommendation to its source
A documentation repair sprint should produce runnable examples rather than longer explanations
Cross-language SDK reviews should compare error behavior before adding convenience methods
Publish a fork compatibility checklist that catches accidental dependencies on the original repository
Collaborative code reviews should leave regression tests the next contributor can extend
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
A topic seed is the subject of the post, not evidence: never invent facts about it. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
